chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadah, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who catches the Imam while he is praying four rak'at, and the Imam has already prayed two rak'at. He said: 'He begins the prayer and enters with him, and reads behind him in the two [remaining] rak'at. He reads in the first Al-Hamd and what he caught of Surah Al-Jumu'ah, and bows with the Imam. And in the second, Al-Hamd and what he caught of Surah Al-Munafiqun, and bows with the Imam. When the Imam sits for Tashahhud, he does not do Tashahhud, but he glorifies [God]. When the Imam gives Salam, he prays two [more] rak'at, glorifies in them, does Tashahhud, and gives Salam.'
ai.seo_question: How should a person complete their prayer if they join the congregation late and miss the first two rak'at?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* outlines the specific fiqh of *muqtadi* (follower) joining late, emphasizing the flexibility of recitation behind the Imam while maintaining the structural integrity of the prayer. It highlights the Shia scholarly distinction between following the Imam in actions (ruku, sujud) and the independent completion of the remaining rak'at, reflecting the jurisprudential principles of *taqlid* in prayer. The detailed instructions ensure the validity of the prayer even when the follower misses the initial recitation phase, underscoring the practical application of Quranic verses on congregational worship.
